facts.statement: Christopher McGowan first described Excalibosaurus in 1986.
facts.quote: It has been described in 1986 by Christopher McGowan.

facts.statement: An almost complete second specimen was collected in 1996 from the same area and purchased by the Royal Ontario Museum.
facts.quote: The second specimen is an almost complete skeleton collected in the same area in 1996, and was purchased by the Royal Ontario Museum.

facts.statement: Christopher McGowan described the second specimen again in 2003.
facts.quote: It was described again by McGowan in 2003.

facts.statement: The largest known specimen of Excalibosaurus reached a total length of 6.528 meters.
facts.quote: The larger specimen has a total length of 6.528 m.

facts.statement: Excalibosaurus is grouped in the family Leptonectidae along with the genera Leptonectes and Eurhinosaurus.
facts.quote: The three genera are grouped in the family Leptonectidae.

facts.statement: Although once thought to be a junior synonym of Eurhinosaurus, the 1996 specimen shows morphological differences like a shorter, broader forefin and a slender body that clearly differentiate the two genera.
facts.quote: It was once thought that Excalibosaurus was a junior synonym of Eurhinosaurus, but the description of the 1996 specimen show many morphological differences such as the shape of the forefin (much shorter and broader in Excalibosaurus), the slender shape of the body, that clearly differentiate the two genera.

facts.statement: Excalibosaurus lived during the Sinemurian stage of the Early Jurassic period in what is now England.
facts.quote: It is characterized by the extreme elongation of the rostrum, with the lower jaw about three-quarters the length of the upper jaw, giving the animal a swordfish-like look. The only known species is Excalibosaurus costini.

facts.statement: Excalibosaurus lived approximately 199.5 to 192.9 million years ago during the Early Jurassic period.
facts.quote: Excalibosaurus (meaning "Excalibur's lizard") is a monotypic genus of marine prehistoric reptiles (ichthyosaurs) that lived during the Sinemurian stage (approximately 199.5 ± 0.3 Ma to 192.9 ± 0.3 Ma (million years ago)) of the Early Jurassic period in what is now England.

facts.statement: Excalibosaurus is known from only two skeletons.
facts.quote: Este animal relativamente raro es conocido de dos esqueletos.

facts.statement: The second specimen is an almost complete skeleton acquired by the Royal Ontario Museum.
facts.quote: El segundo espécimen es un esqueleto casi completo obtenido de la misma área en 1996, y fue adquirido por el Royal Ontario Museum.

facts.statement: The 1996 specimen is estimated to have a body length of 7 meters and a skull length of 1.54 meters.
facts.quote: La longitud corporal estimada del ejemplar de 1996 es de 7 metros con un cráneo de 1.54 metros de largo.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen was much smaller, with a skull length of 0.785 meters and a body length of nearly 4 meters, indicating it was a juvenile.
facts.quote: El espécimen del holotipo era mucho menor, con una longitud craneal de 0.785 m y una longitud corporal de cerca de 4 m, indicando que era un ejemplar juvenil.

facts.statement: Excalibosaurus is closely related to the ichthyosaur genera Leptonectes and Eurhinosaurus.
facts.quote: Excalibosaurus está relacionado de cerca con otros dos géneros de ictiosaurios, Leptonectes del Triásico Tardío (Rhaetiense) al Sinemuriano (Jurásico Temprano) de Inglaterra y Eurhinosaurus del Toarciano (Jurásico Temprano) de Alemania.

facts.statement: These three genera are grouped in the family Leptonectidae and the suborder Eurhinosauria.
facts.quote: Estos tres géneros fueron agrupados en la familia Leptonectidae y el suborden Eurhinosauria.

facts.statement: Excalibosaurus lived from 199.5 to 192.9 million years ago during the Sinemurian stage.
facts.quote: Time range: Sinemurian to Sinemurian (199.5 to 192.9 million years ago)
